intro: Restaurant hosts manage the front door, the waitlist and the mood of guests, a strong start for many service careers. The closest of the 25 careers below is waiting tables, with a 91% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $35,230, which is 13% more than the $31,200 hosts earn.
why_it_works: A Friday night at the host stand means juggling reservations, calming impatient guests and coordinating with servers and the kitchen. O*NET rates service orientation at 3.12 out of 5 for this job. Serving, hotel desk, bartending and airline jobs use the same people skills. Nearly every match pays more, and none needs extra schooling. The skills to build are money handling and decision making.
tips: Move to serving first if you want tips; waiters and waitresses are your closest match.
Flight Attendants earn $63,580, which is 104% more, and airlines train new hires.
Ask to help with scheduling or ordering; food service management pays $69,390.

faq.q: What jobs can former hosts and hostesses do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Waiters and Waitresses (91%), fast food and counter workers (87%) and hotel, motel and resort desk clerks (84%), based on O*NET 31.0. Hotel desk clerks earn $35,070, which is 12% more than the $31,200 host median, and work away from the dinner rush.

faq.q: Which careers for hosts pay more?
faq.a: 23 of the 25 matches pay more than hosting. Food Service Managers earn $69,390 (122% more), gambling services supervisors $63,820 (105% more) and Flight Attendants $63,580 (104% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. BLS medians do not include tips.

faq.q: Do hosts need a degree to change jobs?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches need no more education than hosts and hostesses already have, including all of the top 10. In the closest match, 58% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, and employers train new staff on the job.

The skills that most often need work are managing materials, complex problem solving, managing financial resources and judgment and decision making. Social perceptiveness already rates 3 out of 5 for hosts in O*NET, so learning the business side of a restaurant is the main step up.
